The MDT was and remains an unequal relationship, alongside related agreements such as the Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA). November 11, is Remembrance Day. 

Though this day was founded to abolish war, the way it is marked increasingly serves to glorify war, militarism, and violence. 

Most concerningly, 

school curricula across Canada still make the glorification of war and notions of bravery and sacrifice through military violence central to Remembrance Day.

 













 













 

Download your copy here. 




That’s why World BEYOND War is proud to be launching new educational resources for grades 1-12 that offer an alternative to traditional, militaristic Remembrance Day education, centred around the White Poppy – a symbol meant to recognize all victims of war.

 This pilot project, 

Reframing Remembrance Day: A Handbook for Educators

,

 includes teaching guides, activities, songs, poems, calls to action, and links to further resources.




We invite all educators, parents, youth, and those who know them to 

check out this handbook

, use it, and let us know how you do. This is a brand new pilot project, we are eager to improve it and to hear your feedback and suggestions for what to omit, shift, and add.

author: David Swanson
title: We Can Save Ourselves
content:
By Peter Kuznick and Ivana Nikolić Hughes, World BEYOND War, November 5, 2026




The 1984 British movie 

Threads

 opens with ordinary scenes in Sheffield, England, where a young couple learns they are expecting a baby. The story of their personal life is intertwined with the news of a growing conflict between the United States and the Soviet Union, centered on Iran. We next learn that a nuclear weapon is used in an attack, followed by another. Before long, Sheffield itself is the site of hydrogen bomb detonations, with our protagonists either perishing in the explosions or subsisting under devastating conditions of starvation, civil unrest, radiation-induced and infectious diseases, and freezing temperatures over the coming days, weeks, months, and years. The film ends with the 13-year-old daughter of the young couple from the start of the film giving birth to a deformed clump of flesh months after being raped in a lawless and collapsed society.




Forty-two years after this brilliant movie first gave people in the UK and beyond just a glimpse of the unfathomable consequences of nuclear war, watching the opening scenes is even more grim than it has been in the intervening decades, given just how eerily similar they seem to be to our current moment. the US and Israel continuing to wage war on Iran

author: David Swanson
title: Lakenheath Main Gate Blocked By Protesters: No More Bloody Wars
content:
Close Bases, Europe, Nonviolent Activism, World

[This event was part of the Global Resistance Week to Stop U.S. Imperialism & Genocide happening November 1-7 with 20+ actions at military bases and weapons facilities across 4 countries.]

By No More Bloody War, posted by Lakenheath Alliance For Peace, November 2, 2026

At around 6:45am this morning, on 2nd November 2026, 10 peace protestors have blocked the main gates of RAF Lakenheath, using heavy-duty locks to attach themselves to a car and to each other. They are repeating a similar action taken in April this year by some of the same people today. These protestors come from a diverse range of backgrounds: young and old, and a multitude of faiths and heritages.

The protest has three demands for Burnham’s government:

To shut down US bases residing in the UK.

To stop its support for illegal wars.

Remove US Nuclear weapons from UK soil.

RAF Lakenheath has been blockaded the day before the US midterms to send a firm message that the US military are not welcome in the UK. Thanks to Trumps illegal wars, his approval ratings are at the lowest they’ve been during either of his presidential terms.

The UK is now a legitimate target under international law, due to the UK’s complicity and its participation in allowing US bases to continue operating here. Also, locally, since Lakenheath was established as a US base, it has enacted violence against UK civilians; recent cases include rape, and death from reckless driving (link to the rape/death driving cases).

This nonviolent direct action is in response to war crimes being aided at both Lakenheath and Mildenhall RAF bases. These airbases are owned by the RAF but are used exclusively by the US Air Force, including to support their illegal wars of aggression across the Middle East. This has been particularly highlighted in the recent war against Iran; during which, over 170 fighters and bombers were deployed from RAF Lakenheath, with two being shot down during the conflict.

RAF Mildenhall has typically been used to carry out US refuelling operations during conflicts such as this, and in January three F35i fighters were transferred to Israel via RAF Mildenhall to support Israel’s illegal attacks on Lebanon, as well as the continued genocidal bombing of Palestinian civilians.

It has become apparent that after the midterms, the US and Israel are planning to escalate the war on Iran, a war that began with no evidential or rational basis to class as ‘pre-emptive’. This means the UK will be facing even more danger from the enemies that the US continues to attack. This comes at a time where the threat of nuclear war is at its highest in history and, alongside AI, threatens human extinction within the next two generations.

This nonviolent protest is firmly opposing the nuclear weapons that have been brought back to Lakenheath after an absence of 35 years. By obeying and complying with the demands of the US military complex, the UK has become very closely tied with the nuclear security strategies imposed by the US. Despite another new prime minister, foreign secretary and ambassador to the US, the UK government remains as spineless as ever in the face of the Trump administrations global conquest of terror.

The UK is a signatory to the Conference on Ending the use of Offensive Weapons, and of the Genocide Convention, as well as the European Convention of Human Rights, and so by complying to these US pressures our government is breaching these legally binding international agreements. (ref)

One of the protestors at Lakenheath is a 94 year old human rights lawyer, Margaret Owen, says: “At the age of 94 this is a wonderful opportunity for me to take part in a lock on, which I’d never heard of before, and to stand against the war machines that are destroying millions of lives.”

Rajan Naidu, 75, human rights and social justice campaigner, and a Quaker. It is an incredible and grotesque fact that the British government, in permitting foreign states such as the US and Israel to use British bases like RAF/USAF Lakenheath as launchpads for their pursuit of illegal wars of aggression (e.g. the US war on Iran), war crimes, crimes against humanity (e.g. the illegal occupation, ethnic cleansing, infanticide, genocide of Palestinian people, by the Apartheid regime of Israel), places Britain, squarely and shamefully, in breach of international laws, standards, conventions. British politicians must stop allowing Britain to be exploited as a captive state, of the US, Israel or any other foreign power. Britain must move quickly and decisively to regain its national independence from foreign states like the US and Israel, and begin to behave like a defender, and not gross violator, of human rights/justice/peace.

Shel McDonagh, 39, an organiser of Fairford Action, at another RAF base being used by the US in this illegal war on Iran says: ‘Our government has an obligation for our safety to shut these US bases down now and end it’s support for the US Military. We are now a legitimate target of war, we have seen fuel prices increase by over 40% since the end of February, and the bases contaminate the air, water, and soils around them. The US is not welcome here and these wars do not have public support despite what the media spins. Burnham needs to focus on the future of our communities, not lining the pockets of genocidal and imperialist leaders and industries. If our government won’t follow international law to protect its citizens, it is our moral obligation to take action to shut these bases down.’

Ben Taylor, 32, an ex-soldier says: ‘The UK government needs to stop giving in to the bullying of the US. By giving in, UK citizens suffer, especially the poorest and those most at risk. The resources being used for supporting the US military presence here would make a huge difference in supporting the failing services in our NHS, in schooling and in affordable housing. Instead the UK government puts not just those serving, but also UK citizens here at further risk; and ultimately it continues to be complicit in these unnecessary and childishly impulsive wars’.

Another protestor, Carolyn Gelenter, 68, a Jewish daughter of a Polish Holocaust Survivor and who took part in the action at Lakenheath last April says: ‘The illegal wars continue, the genocide continues. After what my father suffered, I am compelled to participate in whatever form of nonviolent action it takes to stop our government from using tax payers money to aid and abet illegal war and genocide.”

author: David Swanson
title: It’s Time to Ban Autonomous Weapons
content:
Africa, Cameroon Chapter, Chapters, Demilitarization

By Guy Feugap, World BEYOND War’s Africa Organizer, November 1, 2026

As part of the Stop Killer Robots campaign’s Global Week of Action from October 25 to 31, 2026, the Cameroon chapter of World BEYOND War organized a photo action at the Reunification Monument in Yaoundé. This event, held at this symbolic site representing Cameroonians’ aspirations for peace, aimed to draw public attention to the dangers of autonomous weapons and the need to encourage the country to maintain its position and call on other states to permanently ban autonomous weapons. This event is part of a global campaign leading up to the Seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW), scheduled for November 16–20, 2026, in Geneva.

Through this symbolic action, World BEYOND War members in Cameroon are drawing attention to an issue that has now moved beyond the realm of science fiction: the development of weapons systems capable of autonomously selecting and attacking targets. For the members, it is essential to ensure that technological advances do not compromise human life or the fundamental principles of international law; no technology, even when controlled by a human being, is acceptable if its purpose is to kill human beings. Using campaign posters, the participants helped bring to light a major threat to peace, security, and the protection of human life. Beyond the photography, this event was an opportunity to educate chapter members and raise awareness among passersby about the ethical, legal, and humanitarian issues surrounding autonomous weapons, while emphasizing the importance of civic engagement including through signing the Stop Killer Robots campaign petition.

The urgency of this mobilization is underscored by reports of testing and use of autonomous weapons systems in armed conflicts, particularly in Ukraine. The Stop Killer Robots campaign highlights systems capable of autonomously detecting and killing people. It also highlights the use of military tools based on artificial intelligence to propose targets with minimal human validation, like in the contexts of Gaza. Not all of these tools are necessarily autonomous weapons, but they illustrate the risks associated with the increasing automation of military decision-making. When automated systems are deployed in this way in conflicts, it becomes essential to determine how to ensure that no new weapons are produced and put into circulation. The time for debating the technical possibilities of artificial intelligence in the military sphere is over. It is time to establish legally binding international rules to prevent harm and protect humanity from the consequences of autonomy in weapons systems.

The Seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, to be held November 16–20, 2026, in Geneva, presents an opportunity for States to turn several years of diplomatic discussions into concrete negotiations. The Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems, having completed its latest mandate to develop the elements of an international instrument, has seen more than 70 states, as well as the United Nations Secretary-General and the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, acknowledge that the work accomplished provides a sufficient basis to begin negotiations. Furthermore, 130 countries have expressed their support for a legally binding instrument on autonomous weapons systems. In this context, Stop Killer Robots calls on States Parties to adopt, at the Review Conference, a mandate to negotiate a new protocol to the Convention in 2027, with the goal of concluding negotiations within one year. If no agreement is reached in Geneva to launch negotiations, the campaign urges states in favor of legally binding regulations to consider other diplomatic avenues to ensure the process is not stalled.

Cameroon’s position is of particular importance in this effort. As a State Party to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons and a member of the African Group and the Non-Aligned Movement, Cameroon supports the negotiation of a legally binding instrument on autonomous weapons systems. During the March 2026 session of the Group of Governmental Experts, Cameroon noted that the work carried out had led to significant progress and that the evolving text constituted an excellent basis for negotiations toward the adoption of a legally binding instrument. Furthermore, in December 2025, Cameroon voted in favor of United Nations General Assembly Resolution 80/57 on lethal autonomous weapons systems. This resolution underscores the urgency of addressing the humanitarian, legal, security, technological, and ethical concerns raised by these systems. These positions serve as an important foundation for strengthening Cameroon’s diplomatic engagement in Geneva.

As the Review Conference approaches, World BEYOND War Cameroon joins civil society in calling on the Cameroonian government to maintain and strengthen its support for the launch of negotiations on a legally binding instrument. The chapter also encourages other States Parties to the Convention to support a negotiating mandate and to ensure that the instrument to be negotiated simply bans autonomous weapons. The action taken at the Reunification Monument served as a reminder that the issue of autonomous weapons calls upon our responsibility to protect human life and maintain peace. World BEYOND War Cameroon’s message is that states must abolish autonomous weapons systems, because human control does not guarantee that human lives will be saved.

title: The 10 Worst Congressional Excuses for Voting for More Military Spending
content:
Economic Cost, Immorality, Law, Myth of Necessity, North America, What to do

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 30, 2026

Every year for many years now, the bitterly divided, grid-locked, virtually civil-war-waging United States Congress (as it’s commonly depicted) has harmoniously voted for vastly more money in war spending than it had done the year before. Our lords and misrepresentatives are threatening the same again right now.

It’s a heartwarming story of cooperation and understanding, no doubt, but how can you, as an elected official, explain to constituents living third-world lives in a wealthy nation that, not only can you not tax the rich or the corporations, but you also cannot afford to fund education, energy, environment, transportation, retirement, healthcare, or housing because the weapons dealers just want more and more?

The trick, of course, in most cases is to keep your head down and your mouth shut until a bigger military spending bill than last year’s is guaranteed to pass no matter how you vote, and then vote No. You’ll be untouchable. It’s golden. You won’t have publicly organized your colleagues or used various available procedures to actually try to reduce the war spending, but you’ll have an “I voted No” shield, and that’s all you’ll need. Constituents will fall for it without fooling any weapons dealers.

But what if it’s your turn? What if you’ve drawn the short string this year? What if you can either vote Yes or anger your party’s “leader”?

Never fear! That’s what this handy guide is for! Here are 10 popular categories of excuses that have proven effective through the past quarter-century.

You can easily depict an increase to military spending as a decrease if it’s a smaller increase than someone — ideally the president — had initially proposed. This one is in the works right now and may prove very successful. A variation on this is to claim that the bad political party (the one you’re not in) would have gotten a larger increase if you hadn’t hurried or stalled, depending on which party is gaining or losing a majority.

Almost foolproof is the oft-used explanation that you focused your efforts on doing exactly what the peace activists wanted by removing some nasty section from the bill. “You didn’t want the U.S. and Israeli militaries to merge. You said to only vote for the bill if that was removed. We got it removed on condition that we vote for the bill. This is how things work in the real world.” This excuse gets a 5 out of 5 on Yelp. Anyone who objects is a silly dreamer, so you need not address their concerns.

Almost matching the batting record of #2 (removing something) is adding something. It hardly matters how absurd the thing or how out of place in an institution of mass-murder and destruction, as long as it’s humanitarian. Create an agency of environmentally sustainable carpet bombing, or eliminate discrimination against transgendered pilots, or establish a proactive contracting program to minority-owned surveillance companies. Whatever. Anyone who objects will be objecting to that thing you voted for. You should be clear that it is only that thing for which you voted; nothing else exists.

If you cannot use the top three steaming turds of the coming apocalypse, or don’t have time to come up with anything concrete, just fall back on troopism. You voted to fund the troops. Anyone objecting hates the troops, wants the troops left in the wars but their armor and weaponry carefully collected and brought home without them. If you can, grab an actual troop or three to stand in front of and ask one of them to slap you in the face really quickly until there are tears visible in your eyes before the cameras are ready.

Numerous other excuses can work beautifully, depending on the circumstances. There’s always a most-unpopular war among the current wars. Right now, for example, some people are more upset about the crumbs going to the war on Iran than about the mountain of loafs going to the Pentagon in its entirety. So, here’s what you do. You make getting a war powers resolution on Iran vetoed part of a grand bargain in which you vote for the money to create 10 more similar wars. Or you join in a lawsuit against the war on Iran. Or you actually include in the spending bill or elsewhere a ban on spending money on that particular crime — but make clear to everyone that it’s part of a grand bargain on a 4-D chessboard. You voted for increased war money FOR PEACE and so that you could end THE war!

While changing the topic is a losing argument when done too blatantly, it can be very, very effective when done through omission and media saturation. If you can make something else the big story and do something peace-ish on that big thing, you can get huge mileage out of it. For example, you vote for more war money but you also VOTE TO IMPEACH HEGSETH. That doesn’t remove Hegseth, much less the guy whose every whim he obeys, but it’s AWESOME!

Pretty darn powerful, as well, is the futile legislation ploy (FLP). You may vote to increase military spending by 20 percent, but if you are a cosponsor and champion of separate legislation that would reduce military spending by 10 percent, your peace-loving constituents will understand that you are with them.

You don’t actually need me to tell you this. You know it’s there when the time is right. Anyone who objects to your war votes is anti-Semitic. QED.

Sure, you may have voted for increased spending on wars, but you’re in a super-purple district. If you were to give the forces of darkness the chance to label you “weak on defense” then your constituents would end up with a racist, sexist pig voting for increased mass-murder funding in place of you doing it. Which would they rather have?

Thanks for addressing this and we definitely can stop the apocalypse. We’ll be fine if we keep at it. Reply

The Nation had an article last week called How to Stop Trump’s Coup. It brought lessons to the United States from South Korea and was written by Jungmin Choi and by Paul Loeb who had made Choi’s earlier article into the first chapter of his book.

The version in The Nation has been made timely by claiming to offer “lessons for how Americans can counter Donald Trump and his allies if they disrupt or defy the results of November’s midterms,” while the version in the book has been made timeless by being stripped of explicit reference to any application. But the original article in Waging Nonviolence got it right, I think, in suggesting that the emergency was already upon us, that in fact there was no need to wait for a moment of even worse government malfeasance.

By Norbert Byambo Kagosi with Mujib Abid, Peace Voice, October 22, 2026

Forced and involuntary displacement can have many causes. I fled my country for many reasons, including insecurity, persistent conflict, and hatred in my village. In my hometown of Kiliba, in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), life had become unbearable. People could be killed brutally, as if their lives had no value. Nobody knew who would be the next victim or when the violence would strike again.

Completing my diploma in 2018 put a target on my back. Rebels did not want to see someone who had studied and gained an education. What should have been a moment of pride gradually became a source of fear as my life was threatened.

One night, I heard voices outside our house. The people were threatening to kill everyone, saying that nobody would be left alive, not even a child. Those words filled me with terror. They opened the door to my parents’ house and then came directly to the room where I was sleeping. I had no time to think about what to take with me or where I would go. I escaped through a window and ran for my life.

title: Community Dialogue to Advance Disarmament and Peacebuilding in The Gambia
content:
Africa, Africa Projects, Chapters, Gambia Chapter

By Omar Mboob, World BEYOND War Gambia Chapter Coordinator, October 18, 2026

World BEYOND War Gambia chapter organized a Multi-stakeholder community dialogue on disarmament and peace on 17 October 2026, at the National Youth Council Hall in Banjul, The Gambia. The event brought together 20 participants, including youth leaders, students, women representatives, grassroots organizers, and civil society representatives, to discuss the proliferation of small arms and light weapons, community security, nonviolent conflict prevention, and youth participation in peacebuilding. The dialogue took place against the backdrop of security concerns associated with illicit arms trafficking, particularly around the Foni region and the cross-border corridor linking The Gambia and Senegal’s Casamance region. Participants emphasized the importance of peaceful coexistence, community engagement, and constructive dialogue in preventing violence and promoting national development.

A central theme of the dialogue was the need to address the proliferation of weapons while strengthening communities’ capacity to prevent violence. Participants discussed how young people can challenge attitudes that normalize violence, promote nonviolent alternatives, and take an active role in their communities in order to contribute to peacebuilding. title: The One Big Peace Conference and Open Borders
content:
Nonviolent Activism, What to do, Why End War, World

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 16, 2026

Approximately once a day for forever, so approximately 365 times a year, someone proposes to me the same good idea. Hey, they suggest, I’d like to organize one big peace conference and create one big peace movement to unite everyone and be stronger instead of fractured.

I have several answers. First and foremost is: hell yeah, great idea, do it! do it! do it!

Another answer is: there are reasons the 364 other people who’ve said this to me this year have not actually done it, just like the 365 who thought of it last year. It costs lots of money. It’s harder to get people to a conference than to a rally or a protest. There are language barriers. Whoever is in charge of organizing it will be assumed by others to not be totally welcoming of their views. There will be at least some truth to that, since no two people completely agree on everything. If you have this one big conference for everyone in a physical location, as 90 percent of you with this idea want, it will be closer and easier to get to for some people than for others. Maybe we should attempt a regional one for some people. Etc. Etc.

But once a year, I like to focus on a different answer, this one: I don’t have time to do yours for you because I’m already doing it.
